EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation intensified significantly in the last 24 hours with a drone attack originating from Iraq targeting Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline, prompting Saudi Arabia to temporarily shut down the pipeline and Iraq to dismiss a military commander and close border crossings with Iran. Concurrently, Iran reported clashes with armed militants in its southeastern province of Sistan and Baluchestan, while Yemeni forces claimed further battlefield victories and launched missile attacks against multiple Saudi cities. Diplomatic efforts continued at the BRICS summit, where Iranian President Pezeshkian met with UAE and Chinese officials, though US officials alleged Iran used Chinese satellite imagery in a previous attack on a US base in Jordan.

IRAN
Clashes were reported today in Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan Province, near the border with Pakistan, between what Iranian sources described as Baloch separatists or armed militants and local security forces. The IRGC Quds Ground Force claimed to have killed 4 "terrorists" and seized weapons and explosives, while Vahid Online, also citing IRGC, reported that 3 IRGC members (described as "Imam Zaman guards") were killed alongside 4 armed militants. In the political sphere, President Masoud Pezeshkian attended the BRICS summit in New Delhi, meeting with UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed, Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi, Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, and Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Pezeshkian stated that Iran has no issues with its Muslim neighbors, attributing regional discord to US efforts to foster enmity. He also emphasized the necessity of a BRICS role in addressing the Palestinian issue and called for "operational confrontation" against unilateral sanctions. Pezeshkian claimed Iran and Oman would sign an agreement for a joint shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz on Monday, with other Gulf states' foreign ministers present. Ebrahim Azizi, head of the Iranian Parliament’s National Security and Foreign Policy Committee, reiterated that no negotiations with the US would occur until all of Iran’s conditions are met. Internally, there were reports of criticism against former President Hassan Rouhani, with some in "night gatherings" calling him the "rejected devil." The economic situation remains challenging, with reports of Iran's inflation rate reaching 144% (Steve Hanke), the highest since the COVID-19 pandemic, and the price of imported frozen meat increasing by 30% in one month. The US dollar was reported at 237,000 and 236,100 Iranian Tomans by one source. The Telecommunication Company of Iran increased fixed-line to mobile call costs by 45%. A "controlled explosion" was reported in Isfahan. The IRGC Commander, Major General Vahidi, and the Army Commander, Major General Hatami, held a joint meeting to discuss "latest developments on the battlefields," emphasizing the unity and coordination between their forces as key to national security and asserting Iran's military capabilities "far exceed what the enemy had anticipated." The IRGC spokesman also hailed the Yemeni Ansarullah's victories as a "divine victory."

ISRAEL
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced today that Israeli forces, during an operation in the Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon, discovered and removed significant quantities of Iranian-supplied weapons from Hezbollah infrastructure. These caches included dozens of rockets, missiles, drones, anti-tank missiles, mines, and explosives. The IDF reported enhanced readiness for the upcoming Jewish New Year holidays in Judea and Samaria. Politically, Itamar Ben-Gvir's Jewish Power party was reported as the top party among first-time voters, garnering 18% support. Internationally, planned Jewish New Year celebrations on the tourist island of Phuket, Thailand, were canceled following an anti-Israel protest nearby. One source reported a proposal from the Prime Minister (likely Israel's) to Saudi Arabia for Israel to participate in the war against the Houthis in Yemen.

GAZA & WEST BANK
No direct ground operations were reported in Gaza or the West Bank. The humanitarian situation in Gaza was highlighted by images of children walking to school amid rubble. A French public broadcaster removed the replay of a program after actress Adèle Haenel denounced what she called Israel’s genocide in Gaza and France’s complicity, raising concerns about free speech in the West. Israeli military readiness in Judea and Samaria was reported ahead of the Jewish New Year holidays.

LEBANON
Lebanese President Joseph Aoun visited Nabatieh today. Israeli forces conducted a strike in Wadi Zibqin, Lebanon. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu stated that a substantial amount of Iranian-supplied weaponry, including rockets, missiles, drones, and explosives, was discovered and removed from Hezbollah infrastructure in Ali al-Taher heights in southern Lebanon.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The Iraqi government confirmed that drone attacks on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline on Thursday originated from Iraqi territory, specifically Maysan province. Following this, the Iraqi Prime Minister's office dismissed a military commander overseeing operations in Maysan province and ordered investigations into security breaches at border crossings. Iraq subsequently closed the Shalamcheh, Sheeb, and Mandali border crossings with Iran, though Shalamcheh and Chazabeh were temporarily reopened for 2-3 hours to allow stranded travelers to return. Iraqi officials stated these measures were temporary and aimed at addressing "administrative and security arrangements" and "security breaches/violations." The Islamic Resistance in Iraq, while expressing pride in Yemeni victories, denied responsibility for the Saudi pipeline attack, stating it was a "badge of honor they don't claim," and warned against "Zionist-American plots" to destabilize Iraq. Iraqi religious leader Moqtada al-Sadr called for unity and cautioned against provocations. Reports indicated a fuel crisis in Anbar and other Iraqi provinces, while US military transport planes were observed landing in Erbil and intense US drone activity in the Samawah desert. In Syria, a weapons depot exploded in the Damascus countryside, and an unknown explosion was heard in Damascus.
Regarding Yemen, Iranian sources (Press TV, IRGC) lauded the Ansarullah movement for taking control of strategic islands around the Bab al-Mandeb Strait, calling it a "divine victory." Yemeni forces celebrated battlefield victories, recapturing areas from Saudi-backed forces and seizing US-made military equipment. The Yemeni Armed Forces announced they would show footage of a military operation called "Allah is Mightier and More Punishing" and warned civilians to avoid the Taiz-Al-Makha and Al-Makha-Dhu Bab roads due to bombing in a "kill zone." Saudi Arabia reported multiple cities, including Khamis Mushait, Abha, Sharurah, and Taif, were targeted by Yemeni forces with missiles and that a large fire continued for a third day at the Khurais oil field after Yemeni targeting. Trump claimed the Houthis had contacted the US, stating they did not want to fight American forces. A Yemeni official, however, claimed the Houthi operation was prepared for months and closely directed by Iranians on the ground. The Russian Ambassador to Yemen reiterated support for de-escalation and peace efforts.

GULF STATES
Saudi Arabia's East-West crude oil pipeline was hit by drones on Thursday, confirmed by the Saudi Foreign Ministry to have originated from Iraq. The pipeline was shut down as a precautionary measure, resulting in temporary disruption of oil flow and some injuries. Saudi Arabia announced it "preferred not to respond at this stage" to the attacks but reserved its right to take all measures to protect its sovereignty and security. Kuwait declared its support for Saudi Arabia's actions to protect its sovereignty and security. The Khurais oil field was reported to have continuous fires for the third consecutive day following alleged targeting by Yemeni forces, and a large fire was observed at the Saudi Electricity Company in Abha. A US official indicated Riyadh signaled a willingness to launch a major military operation against the Houthis, even unilaterally. The CENTCOM commander reportedly visited Saudi Arabia to discuss developments in Yemen.
The UAE's Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed met with Iranian President Pezeshkian on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit, a notable diplomatic engagement amid regional tensions. Germany and the UAE issued a joint statement condemning "attacks by the Islamic Republic on the United Arab Emirates and other countries in the region, including attacks on civilian infrastructure." Algeria announced it cut diplomatic ties with the UAE.
US lawmakers accused Qatar of utilizing Indian hacking networks to target opponents and critics, including those involved with the World Cup hosting and a former US House Intelligence Committee chair's family. They urged the US Commerce Department to sanction several companies linked to these hacking networks, including BellTrox, Cyberroot, and Epiin.
Regarding the Strait of Hormuz, Iranian President Pezeshkian announced that Iran and Oman would sign a joint shipping route agreement on Monday. Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman stated the Strait remains under Iran's full control and blamed the US for regional maritime insecurity and rising global fuel prices. Trump made unverified claims that the US "very powerfully" controls the Strait of Hormuz and is "destroying 25 boats daily." Unverified reports also mentioned two explosions heard in the Strait of Hormuz and a cruise missile launch by the IRGC from Sirik towards the Strait.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Saudi Oil Pipeline Attack and Iraqi Response:** Saudi Arabia's East-West oil pipeline was hit by drones originating from Iraq on Thursday, leading to its temporary shutdown and reports of injuries. In response, Iraq's Prime Minister dismissed a military commander from Maysan province (the alleged origin point of the drones) and initiated investigations. Saudi Arabia stated it would "not respond at this stage" but reserved its right to act.
2.  **Iraq-Iran Border Closures:** Following the pipeline attack, Iraq closed the Shalamcheh, Sheeb, and Mandali border crossings with Iran. Shalamcheh and Chazabeh were later temporarily reopened for a few hours to allow stranded travelers to return. Iraqi officials cited security breaches and administrative measures for the closures.
3.  **Iran-UAE Diplomatic Meeting:** Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian met with UAE Crown Prince Sheikh Khaled bin Mohamed bin Zayed on the sidelines of the BRICS Summit in New Delhi, indicating continued high-level diplomatic engagement despite regional tensions.
4.  **Clashes in Saravan, Iran:** Intense clashes occurred in Saravan, Sistan and Baluchestan Province, between Iranian security forces/IRGC and armed militants, resulting in casualties on both sides (4 militants and 3 IRGC members, according to an IRGC-linked source).
5.  **Yemeni Houthi Advances and Attacks on Saudi Arabia:** Yemeni Ansarullah was praised by the IRGC for gaining control over strategic islands in the Bab al-Mandeb Strait. Yemeni forces celebrated battlefield victories, and Saudi Arabia reported multiple cities (Khamis Mushait, Abha, Sharurah, Taif) were targeted by Yemeni missile attacks.
6.  **Israeli Weapon Discovery in Lebanon:** Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that a large cache of Iranian-supplied weaponry was found and removed from Hezbollah infrastructure in Ali al-Taher heights, southern Lebanon, by Israeli forces.
7.  **US Accusations of Chinese Satellite Imagery to Iran:** US officials alleged that Iran obtained high-resolution Chinese satellite imagery of a US base in Jordan before a July 17 missile strike that killed three American troops, creating potential for US-China friction.
8.  **Iran's BRICS Diplomacy and Hormuz Agreement:** Iranian President Pezeshkian, during the BRICS summit, advocated for a robust BRICS response to unilateral sanctions and announced an impending agreement with Oman for a joint shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks remain high, particularly with the unretaliated drone attack on Saudi oil infrastructure from Iraqi territory, which could provoke future Saudi responses against non-state actors in Iraq or Yemen. Potential for a major Saudi military operation against the Houthis in Yemen, as suggested by a US official, poses a significant risk for broader conflict. Active flashpoints include the Yemen-Saudi border, Red Sea maritime routes, internal unrest in Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province, and the southern Lebanon-Israel border. Military postures are hardening, with Iraqi actions to control armed groups and Iranian Army and IRGC commanders emphasizing unity and a strong retaliatory capacity. Trump's rhetoric about Iran being "two weeks" from a nuclear weapon, though unverified, signals continued US pressure and concern over Iran's nuclear program, particularly following a hardline Iranian parliament member's call for NPT withdrawal and nuclear tests. The alleged use of Chinese satellite imagery by Iran in the Jordan attack adds a layer of geopolitical tension between the US and China. Unverified reports of explosions and missile launches in the Strait of Hormuz indicate continued instability in that crucial waterway.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture, as articulated by President Trump, includes accusing Iran of responsibility for the Saudi pipeline attack, claiming the Houthis do not wish to fight the US, and making unverified assertions about US control over the Strait of Hormuz and Iran being "two weeks" from nuclear weapons. US officials also flagged Iran's alleged use of Chinese satellite imagery in the Jordan attack. The US House Rules Committee is considering the "Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026." US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth made strong statements about US military actions against Iran, claiming Iranian leaders were killed and military capabilities destroyed, while calling for the arming of the Iranian people. The US State Department maintains regular contact with regional allies regarding Yemen.
Among **Gulf States**, Saudi Arabia chose not to retaliate immediately for the pipeline attack but reserved its right to do so, while Kuwait expressed support for Saudi Arabia's sovereignty and security measures. The UAE engaged diplomatically with Iran's President at BRICS, but also, jointly with Germany, condemned Iranian attacks on regional civilian infrastructure. Qatar faces accusations from US lawmakers of using Indian hacking networks to target opponents, with calls for sanctions on related companies.
**EU members** saw Germany and the UAE issue a joint condemnation of Iranian attacks. France's public broadcaster removed a program after an actress spoke out against the "Israeli genocide in Gaza." Sweden's Justice Ministry stated that Iran threatens Sweden's security.
**Russia** saw President Putin warn that European forces in Ukraine would mean direct war with Russia, while the Russian Ambassador to Yemen voiced support for de-escalation and peace efforts there. Russia also conducted a drone missile strike on Odesa and Chornomorsk in Ukraine.
**China's** President Xi Jinping attended the BRICS summit, his first visit to India since 2019, stating China's readiness to help reduce Middle East tensions. Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with his Iranian counterpart. The alleged provision of satellite imagery to Iran by Chinese entities is a source of tension with the US.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several contradictions and unverified claims exist within the intelligence feed. The exact casualties in the Saravan clashes are inconsistent, with various sources reporting different numbers of IRGC members and armed militants killed. Trump's claims regarding US control over the Strait of Hormuz ("destroying 25 boats daily") and Iran being "two weeks" from a nuclear weapon are highly unverified and likely exaggerated for rhetorical effect. Similarly, reports of "two explosions" and an IRGC cruise missile launch in the Strait of Hormuz from the "omid dana" channel lack independent verification and should be treated with extreme caution, as this source frequently publishes sensational and unconfirmed claims. The status of Iraqi border crossings with Iran appears fluid and somewhat contradictory, with different reports on which crossings are open, closed, or temporarily reopened, suggesting a dynamic situation or varied reporting. There is also a reporting gap regarding the full context behind Algeria cutting diplomatic ties with the UAE. Propaganda indicators are evident in both Iranian state-linked media (e.g., Press TV emphasizing US "aggression" and Iran's "resistance") and certain opposition channels (e.g., "omid dana" and "kianmeli1" using highly charged language against the Iranian regime and promoting specific narratives, sometimes with speculative or provocative content). The internal political claim by "omid dana" regarding the promotion of Hassan Rouhani by "part of the regime" on Twitter is unverified and speculative.
